title: Visualizing Angiogenesis by Multiphoton Microscopy In Vivo in Genetically Modified 3D-PLGA/nHAp Scaffold for Calvarial Critical Bone Defect Repair
protocol: Clone pdgf-b cDNA into a lentiviral expression vector pLenti6/5-eGFP downstream of the cytomegalovirus promoter using Spe I and Sal I restriction sites.
Co-transfect HEK-293FT cells with virus packaging plasmids (pLP1, pLP2, and pVSV-G) using the standard calcium phosphate method with chloroquine (final concentration: 25 µM).
Harvest 500 mL of virus-containing supernatant after 48 hours of transfection.
Filter the harvested supernatant through a filter (0.45 μm).
Concentrate viral particles by ultracentrifugation at 89,000 x g for 2 hours.
Resuspend concentrated viral particles in 200 µL of phosphate-buffered saline (PBS).
Aliquot resuspended viral particles and store at -80 °C.
Dissolve 20 g of PLGA in 20 mL of 1,4-dioxane to form a homogeneous solution.
Add 2 g of nanosized HAp powder to the solution.
Stir the mixed solution vigorously at 1,500 rpm for 16 hours using a magnetic stirrer.
Fabricate porous PLGA/nHAp scaffolds using a 3D low-temperature printer according to a predesigned model.
Vacuum freeze-dry the scaffolds at -78 °C under 45 Pa vacuum for 48 hours.
Soak the scaffolds in 75% ethanol solution for 1 hour.
Rinse the scaffolds with PBS twice after soaking.
Incubate each scaffold with 10 µL of LV particles at 37 °C for 2 hours in a humidified incubator.
Rinse the scaffolds again with PBS twice to remove unbound LV particles.
Snap-freeze the LV particle-coated scaffolds in liquid nitrogen.
Lyophilize the scaffolds once more.
Store the LV particle-coated scaffolds at -80 °C for future use.
Incubate 3D scaffolds carrying LV-eGFP in 1 mL of complete DMEM at 37 °C with shaking for 5 days.
Take a 1 mL sample every 12 hours from 12 to 120 hours post-incubation.
Replace the medium by adding 1 mL of fresh medium after each sample collection.
Use collected media to transduce HEK293T cells by co-incubating for 48 hours.
Measure the number of bioactive LV particles by determining GFP-positive HEK293T cells via flow cytometry.
Before transducing HEK293T cells, remove culture medium and rinse cells twice with PBS.
Add collected media containing lentivirus to wells (1 mL/well) for culturing with HEK293T cells at 37 °C in a humidified incubator for 48 hours.
Prepare BMSCs expressing tomato fluorescent protein (BMSCs-T) before migration assay.
Prepare BMSCs expressing PDGF-BB protein (BMSCs-P) before migration assay.
Perform BMSC migration assay using a Boyden chamber with a 24-well plate and polycarbonate filters of 8 µm pore size.
Place 0.5 mL of BMSCs transfected with LV expressing tomato fluorescent protein (BMSCs-T) in the upper chambers.
Place 0.5 mL of BMSCs transfected with LV expressing PDGF-BB protein (BMSCs-P) in the lower chambers.
Add 500 µL to the lower compartment of each well for six groups: blank control, FBS control, PDGF-BB control, PDGF-BB seize group, BMSC group, and BMSCs-P group.
Incubate for 48 h at 5% CO2 and 37 °C in a humidified incubator.
Remove the migrated cells on the lower chamber side using a cell scraper.
Resuspend the migrated cells with 2 mL of PBS.
Quantify the number of migrated BMSCs-T by flow cytometry.
Enroll a total of 42 male mice for the calvarial bone defect experiment.
Randomly divide the mice into three groups with fourteen in each group.
Administer sodium pentobarbital intraperitoneally at 50 mg/kg to anesthetize the animals.
Remove fur from the head using depilatory paste.
Clean the head skin with a 75% alcohol solution.
Fix the head of each mouse with a stereotactic instrument.
Make an initial incision with a scalpel.
Enlarge the incision with scissors to create a 1-cm linear skin incision.
Scrape the periosteum from the bone of the cranium using a sterile cotton swab.
Use a trephine burr to create a 4 mm-diameter critical-size defect on the left side of the calvaria.
Transplant the scaffold into the bone defect site.
Use ophthalmic forceps to move the periosteum back gently to cover the surgical site.
Suture the incised skin with three stitches per cm.
Administer buprenorphine at 0.1 mg/kg to relieve pain post-operatively.
Maintain body temperature with a heating pad until the animal awakens.
Feed animals with food and water after surgery.
Record activity every day until the end of the test.
Intravenously inject FITC-conjugated 250 kD dextran at 10 mg/mL in saline into mice for imaging.
Assemble multiphoton microscopy (MPM) system for TPEF and SHG imaging.
Anesthetize animals with an intraperitoneal injection of pentobarbital sodium at 50 mg/kg.
Immobilize the animals on a heating plate to maintain body temperature at 37 °C.
Use 3.0% isoflurane gas in 100% oxygen for anesthesia during imaging.
Intraperitoneally inject saline at 200 µL/animal to prevent dehydration before imaging.
Tune the femtosecond Ti-Sapphire laser to 860 nm.
Create a 512 x 512 µm sampling area by scanning a pair of galvo mirrors.
Focus the excitation beam into the sample using an NA1.0 water-immersion objective lens.
Collect the backscattered TPEF/SHG signal using the same objective lens.
Split the induced TPEF and SHG signals from the excitation laser using a dichroic mirror at 685 nm.
Purify the split signals with a 680-nm short-pass filter.
Conduct the TPEF and SHG signals to a spectrograph via a fiber bundle.
Record the signal in 16 consecutive spectral bands from 400 nm to 600 nm at 12.5-nm intervals using linear array PMTs on the spectrograph.
Detect TPEF and SHG signals simultaneously and separate them in spectral domains.
Control the imaging depth for 3D imaging using an axial motor.
Set the area of each image to 512 x 512 μm.
Set the depth interval to 2 μm (for control group, set it to 5 μm).
Image 5 sites on each defect for statistically significant data collection.
Distribute and select imaging sites evenly and randomly along the defect.
Scan 5 sites on each defect to collect statistically significant data to measure vessel formation.
Use scanning sites evenly and randomly distributed along the defect.
For the control group, have the field of view cover both the original bone area and the edge of the defect.
For the PH and PHp groups, have the FOV on the implanted scaffold.
Make a 1-cm linear skin incision using a scalpel.
Suture the open skin to the fixation to reveal the transplantation site.
Place a drop of water between the dipping lens and transplants to form a water glass.
Acquire image stacks every 12 s over a 2 h imaging period.
Display and analyze volumetric data using a custom MATLAB program.
Quantify the blood vessel areas with ImageJ software.
Harvest implanted scaffolds and tissues from the experimental mice at 2, 4, and 8 weeks post-operation.
Take control group samples (n = 4) at the same time points from adjacent bone tissue.
Euthanize the mice with CO2 inhalation at each time point (2, 4, and 8 weeks).
Dissect the calvaria from the euthanized mice.
Remove and harvest the implanted scaffolds from the dissected calvaria.
Extract total RNA from each sample using a commercial reagent according to the manufacturer's protocol.
Reverse-transcribe the extracted RNA into cDNA using the Reverse Transcription Kit following the manufacturer's protocol.
Perform quantitative real-time PCR using the SYBR Green Detection System.
Use primers listed in Table 1 for the target genes pdgfb, vWF, VEGFR2, and β-actin.
Euthanize mice with CO2 inhalation at 8 weeks post-operation.
Dissect the skull for microCT imaging of the bone defect region.
Use scanning parameters: 9 µm resolution, Al 0.5 mm filter, 50 kV voltage, and 142 µA current.
Reconstruct all imaging data using commercial software provided by the company.
Calibrate the scans using the calibration function of a CTAn software.
